newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse/CBS acquiring TNN, CMT networks from Gaylord.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse/CBS acquiring TNN, CMT networks from Gaylord.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp., essentially completing its transition to a broadcasting company, said Monday it agreed to buy two country music cable television networks from Gaylord Entertainment Co. for $1.5 billion in stock.

Westinghouse, which acquired CBS Inc. in late 1995 and is spinning off its industrial manufacturing businesses, said it had a definitive agreement to acquire the domestic and overseas operations of The Nashville Network (TNN) and the North American operations of Country Music Television (CMT) network.

Pittsburgh-based Westinghouse, which is also acquiring the Infinity Broadcasting Corp. to add to its CBS and Group W radio networks, said the deal with Gaylord includes about $50 million of working capital.

Shareholders of Gaylord Entertainment, based in Nashville, will receive $1.55 billion in Westinghouse common stock in the transaction, which is intended to be tax-free to Gaylord and its shareholders, Westinghouse said.
The number of shares to be issued by Westinghouse will depend on the average price of its stock during a trading period just prior to the closing of the transaction, the company said.

"This acquisition is an important strategic move that expands the reach and scope of our media businesses ... and is immediately accretive to shareholders," Westinghouse Chairman Michael H. Jordan said in a statement.

"Having built a preeminent radio group with the Infinity acquisition and now establishing a strong position in cable, we complete the major actions on the investment priorities we established at the time of the CBS acquisition," Jordan added.

Gaylord Monday reported that its net income for the quarter rose 22 percent to $27.4 million, or 28 cents a share, from $22.4 million, or 23 cents a share, while revenues expanded by 11 percent to $194.0 million from $174.7 million.

For all of 1996 Gaylord said its net income grew 21 percent to $131.2 million, or $1.34 a share, from $108.4 million, or $1.11 a share, as revenues rose 6 percent to $747.2 million from $707.5 million.

Gaylord, which also owns the Grand Ole Opry, the Opryland park and Opryland Hotel in Nashville, said revenues from its two cable networks increased 20 percent to $84.3 million in the quarter and by 17 percent to $331.8 million for the year.

Westinghouse and Gaylord have cooperated in cable programming since 1982, with Gaylord providing the programming content of TNN and CMT and Westinghouse's Group W Satellite Communications providing services like affiliate relations, advertising sales and marketing.
"Westinghouse/CBS is taking ownership of two of the most valuable cable networks in the industry," Gaylord Chairman Edward L. Gaylord said.

"For some time we have seen consolidation in the cable broadcasting industry. Our judgment is that further growth of TNN and CMT can best be served as part of a larger media company that can use its leverage to help take these country music and country lifestyle networks to an even higher level of visibility."

Westinghouse said that as part of the transaction, Mr. Gaylord, members of his family and certain shareholders, who together hold more than 60 percent of the voting power of Gaylord's stock, agreed to support the transaction.

TNN and CMT complement Westinghouse's CBS television and radio properties. CBS also owns eight country music radio stations in major U.S. markets, including WUSN-FM Chicago, the most listened-to country music station in the nation.
"Our ownership of TNN and CMT will make us key players in country music and country lifestyle businesses, cable programming, and multichannel distribution," Jordan said.
"We see opportunities to expand those franchises, to develop programming jointly for broadcast and cable, and to cross-promote all our media properties."

Currently reaching over 70 million households in the United States and Canada, TNN is the second-largest North American cable network and the eighth-largest in the United States. CMT has 38 million subscribers in the United States.

Also included in the merger are CMT Canada, a joint venture with Shaw Cable of Canada, several cable production companies, and NASCAR Thunder, a chain of retail stores themed on NASCAR stock car racing.

The transaction is subject to several conditions, including regulatory approvals, the receipt of a ruling from the Internal Revenue Service and the approval of Gaylord Entertainment's shareholders, Westinghouse said.
Westinghouse's stock closed Friday at $17.875 on the New York Stock Exchange while Gaylord Entertainment ended the week at $25.375, also on the NYSE.
